about: Stages and timing for the deliverability-recovery playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: trend
stages.do: Trend delivery, bounces, complaints and unsubscribes by week and find where problems come from; add them as findings.

stages.name: frequency
stages.do: Measure how many messages customers get and where opt-outs climb; add over-messaging as a finding with the cap it recommends.

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.

stages.name: reach
stages.do: Measure who can be reached with consent and how consent is moving; add gaps as findings, then choose the finding a sunset or re-permission flow will address.

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.

stages.name: launch
stages.do: Clone a proven sunset or re-permission scenario as a draft after its own yes, or find there is nothing to clone.

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.
no finding calls for a sunset or re-permission flow; caps and suppression are set in the Engagement UI.

stages.name: adapt
stages.do: Build the flow from the outline when there was nothing to clone, or make the launch fix list's step changes in the draft, each after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.
no finding calls for a sunset or re-permission flow; caps and suppression are set in the Engagement UI.
the user stopped before any flow was made.

stages.name: test
stages.do: Optionally add an A/B split to the draft after its own yes (a holdout fits a sunset flow: a share that stays in today's sending), before QA so QA sees the split; record no_test, or skip the stage, when the user doesn't want a test.

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.
no finding calls for a sunset or re-permission flow; caps and suppression are set in the Engagement UI.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
no flow was built.

stages.name: qa
stages.do: QA the draft, with its A/B split if the test stage added one, until it is GO; a NO-GO fix goes back through the adapt stage's write skill (engagement-scenario-builder), with its own yes, and is QA'd again. Then wait for the user to switch it on in the Engagement UI, record the day it started, and record the switch-on as a change (source engagement-ui).

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.
no finding calls for a sunset or re-permission flow; caps and suppression are set in the Engagement UI.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
no flow was built.

stages.name: ab-read-out
stages.do: Read out the test stage's split on its agreed primary metric: call the winner, keep it running until a later date, or stop as inconclusive. The user acts on the verdict in the Engagement UI.

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.
no finding calls for a sunset or re-permission flow; caps and suppression are set in the Engagement UI.
the user stopped before any flow was made.
no flow was built.
the flow was never switched on.
no A/B split was added, so there is no test to read out.
the test stage was skipped, so there is no test to read out.

stages.name: recheck
stages.do: Trend deliverability again and compare the weeks since the flow started with the weeks before.

skip_when.reason: deliverability is within its guard-rails and not drifting, so there is nothing to recover.
no finding calls for a sunset or re-permission flow; caps and suppression are set in the Engagement UI.

notes.recheck_after_days: Days after the qa stage finishes (the day the user switched the flow on) before the recheck stage is due. deliverability-trend pools its last 4 whole weeks (recent_weeks in its rules) against the earlier weeks, so after 28 days the recent pool is all after the start.
notes.readout_after_days: Days after the flow started (the qa stage's done date) before the ab-read-out stage is due. engagement-ab-test-setup sizes a test in whole weeks and never below its min_test_days, which engagement-experiment-readout uses too; 14 matches that minimum. When the test stage agreed a later end date, the readout says keep running: record keep_running with that date.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then. keep_running is the ab-read-out stage's wait, when the test needs more customers or days; inconclusive is its way out when the test never reaches its sample.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes; skips don't cascade, so each stage lists every earlier outcome that ends the run). The adapt and qa stages are not in the original proposal: scenario-template-launcher never edits its clone, hands flows with nothing to clone to engagement-scenario-builder, and hands every clone to scenario-qa; and the flow must be switched on, with its start date recorded, before the recheck can measure it. Frequency caps and suppression found by the first three stages are set by the user in the Engagement UI: no skill writes frequency policies. The test stage is optional: engagement-ab-test-setup adds an A/B split (a message, holdout or timing test) to the draft before the qa stage, so scenario-qa checks the split too, and records its write from its plan and verify files. When the user doesn't want a test, they skip the stage (or it records no_test), and status then offers ab-read-out as a skip. ab-read-out (engagement-experiment-readout) reads the split out before the recheck stage, so the controlled answer comes first.
